sentences.text: Orr also claims that the idea of the tabula rasa is dead, and Pinker is kicking a dead horse.
sentences.label: human

sentences.text: But then Orr does something strange: he turns around and defends the tabula rasa.
sentences.label: AI

sentences.text: Not on scientific grounds — he has already conceded those — but on ethical ones.
sentences.label: AI

sentences.text: Why does Orr think we should preserve an idea he himself regards as empirically discredited?
sentences.label: AI

sentences.text: Because it has had some good _ethical_ consequences.
sentences.label: human

sentences.text: He muses, 'if [Pinker's anti-blank slate] views had held from the time of Locke .
sentences.label: human

sentences.text: would the liberal ethic Pinker reflexively reaches for be there?'
sentences.label: AI

sentences.text: Orr goes on to let us know that he thinks the tabula rasa idea is actually synonymous with liberal values _in_general_.
sentences.label: human

sentences.text: He even decides to call them 'Blank Slate liberal values', to coin a phrase in his last sentence.
sentences.label: human

sentences.text: And he leaves off the review with the very strong implication that we simply can't do without the tabula rasa, because that would be to abandon our values.
sentences.label: human

sentences.text: This is simply absurd.
sentences.label: human

sentences.text: Using the same fallacy, any person of faith can argue the existence of God, on the strange claim that without a strong belief in God throughout many of the cultures and times of human history, would love and charity be there at all?
sentences.label: human

sentences.text: Without Jesus Christ, would 'the liberal ethic Pinker [err, Orr] reflexively reaches for be there?'
sentences.label: human

sentences.text: The idea of God may or may not correspond to something, but the ethical consequences of believing in God have no bearing whatsoever on the validity of the idea.
sentences.label: human

sentences.text: The idea of the tabula rasa, unlike the idea of God, happens to admit evidence -- and the evidence is getting very clear.
sentences.label: human

sentences.text: Pinker's book is, as Orr points out, kicking a dead horse (though it's one that many nonscientists in the humanities do still ride.)
sentences.label: human

sentences.text: It's weird that Orr thinks that to save western ethics he, too, needs to saddle up that utopian pony for one last turn around the grounds.
sentences.label: human

sentences.text: This is hardly the way to argue with the Pinkerites, or with anyone else, for that matter.
sentences.label: human
